acceptance_criteria.criterion: Calling delete() removes the chunk file
Calling delete() on a non-existent file does not raise
The writer is properly closed before deletion

summary: Added `ChunkWriter.delete()` method to `orchestrator/src/utils/chunk_writer.py`. The method closes the writer first (delegating to the idempotent `close()`), then calls `Path.unlink()` on the chunk file. `FileNotFoundError` is silently swallowed; other `OSError`s are logged at DEBUG level and swallowed — matching the existing error-handling pattern in `write_chunk()` and `close()`.

Added 6 tests in `TestDelete` class in `orchestrator/tests/test_chunk_writer.py`, covering all 3 acceptance criteria: file removal, graceful no-op on missing file, and writer closure before deletion. All 52 tests in test_chunk_writer.py pass.

comments.note: No observations — code in the touched files is clean and consistent.

summary: All 3 ACs verified: delete() removes file, gracefully handles missing file, and closes writer before deletion. 52/52 test_chunk_writer.py tests pass.
4 additional edge-case stress tests passed: delete before first write (lazy-open), delete after context manager exit, idempotent multi-call, and write_chunk after delete (safe no-op).

comments.note: No observations — implementation is clean, idiomatic, and consistent with existing error-handling patterns in ChunkWriter.close() and write_chunk(). All edge cases (lazy-open before first write, post-context-manager, idempotency, write after delete) behaved correctly.

summary: Reviewed orchestrator/src/utils/chunk_writer.py (delete() method, ~10 lines) and orchestrator/tests/test_chunk_writer.py (TestDelete class, 6 tests). All 3 acceptance criteria verified.

delete() correctly sequences close() before unlink(). close() is idempotent so the close-before-delete pattern is safe regardless of prior state. FileNotFoundError is silently swallowed; other OSErrors are logged at DEBUG and swallowed — consistent with write_chunk() and close() error-handling conventions.

Path.unlink(missing_ok=True) would be marginally more idiomatic (Python 3.8+, project requires 3.11+) but the explicit except pattern is consistent with the surrounding code. Style choice, not a defect.

Tests cover: file removal, non-existent file no-op, writer-close-before-delete invariant, open-writer deletion, post-close deletion, idempotent double-delete. QA edge cases (delete before first write, context manager, post-delete write_chunk) also passed.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/utils/chunk_writer.py delete(): Python 3.11+ is required by the project, so Path.unlink(missing_ok=True) is available. It would reduce the 3-line try/except/pass to 1 line and is the idiomatic 3.8+ pattern. However, the current explicit `except FileNotFoundError: pass` is consistent with the surrounding error-handling style (close() uses explicit `except OSError`), so this is a style choice, not a defect.

orchestrator/tests/test_chunk_writer.py TestDelete: The `except OSError as exc: log.debug(...)` branch in delete() has no test (would require mocking Path.unlink to raise a non-FileNotFoundError). This matches the testing philosophy for write_chunk() and close() in the same file — OS-level fault injection is not exercised. Acceptable gap, consistent with existing test coverage posture.

[documentation-forward] orchestrator/src/utils/chunk_writer.py delete(): The docstring references 'stream retry' as the intended use context but this is a forward reference to WP-004 integration. Once WP-004 is complete, the public API docs / module docstring should be updated to document the delete() → fresh-file → retry pattern as a first-class usage pattern alongside the basic write/close usage example.
